prompts.title: NEXT: rig accepted body; Hot Walk + sway
prompts.text:
CATHEXIS — first rig and motion tests

Use the owner-accepted Cathexis_Body_v2_50k (51,034 triangles). Keep the unrigged visual master. Do not regenerate her body, costume, materials or proportions for each animation.

Also export a tangent-space normal map matched to this 50k mesh and its UVs, without changing the accepted geometry or base color. The master normal map is not automatically compatible with this remesh. Report if a matched map cannot be exported; this does not prevent a diagnostic rig test.

Stage 2 is closed: no further porcelain expressions, mechanical inserts, half-mask models or facial-expression rig are requested. Rig the BODY ONLY, retaining its complete original mechanical face. Our app will fit the existing full Grace mask or its locally cut half over that head, or leave the face exposed. Do not delete, hollow, smooth away or replace the original face. Do not attach or merge Grace into the body export.

Create a Mixamo-compatible humanoid rig in a clean neutral A-pose. The complete mechanical face, crown and grouped head attachments should follow the head rigidly; torso reactor follows the torso and hip canisters follow the pelvis. Preserve the head shape and report its exact exported joint name and neutral transform so we can calibrate a rigid Grace attachment. Do not add facial blendshapes, moving jaws or expression bones for this prototype. Eye glow is controlled by our app. Dynamic hair cleanup can happen offline.

Important: skirt and hair must not weld the legs together or become uncontrolled rubber. If your rigging tool cannot separate or sensibly weight these parts, report the limitation and provide the neutral export for offline cleanup. Do not replace the distinctive costume with generic clothing. We can add dedicated skirt/hair bones and rigid plate weighting offline.

Preserve the existing five-finger hand geometry. Report the ACTUAL exported finger bones and weighting. If only hand/wrist bones exist, say that explicitly; this does not block the rig test or motion bank. Do not regenerate hands to satisfy a finger-rig requirement. Detailed finger poses and physical Grace removal/reseating are optional offline work later.

First apply ONLY Hot Walk (106) and Happy_Sway_Standing (415). Export both for review before expanding the bank. After those pass, add Mirror_Viewing (48) and Head_Hold_in_Pain (391). The four staged tests are:
1. Hot Walk — our ONLY approved locomotion gait; the prior exported source is Confident_Walk, catalog Action 106. Use that exact source as the first comparison. Keep Hot Walk as our label and retain the source ID/name. If your UI label differs, report the mapping.
2. Happy_Sway_Standing — Action 415. Test relaxed presence, weight shifts, skirt and heel clearance. Do not assume the source is already a seamless idle loop.
3. Mirror_Viewing — Action 48. Test hand/head/face and hair clearance; not yet a finished mask-change animation.
4. Head_Hold_in_Pain — Action 391. Audition head-holding frustration from the conveyor art; test crown, hair and hand clearance. A pain source label does not impose an injury state.

A diagnostic rest pose is required. She NEVER runs and has NO alert state. Do not request ordinary walk/run/alert clips. If the tool automatically bundles them, label them excluded and report that; they must not enter the game bank. No regular worker walk or generic breathing idle as a silent fallback.

Export each test as a textured GLB with the RIGGED CHARACTER INCLUDED, plus FBX. Keep a separate neutral rigged GLB/FBX. Use the Mixamo skeleton template consistently. If exporting all added animations as one file is supported, also supply it, but keep individual exports so missing clips can be checked.

Use clear aliases:
Cathexis_Body_v2_Rigged_APose
cathexis_hot_walk_106_source
cathexis_mirror_48_source
cathexis_sway_415_source
cathexis_head_hold_391_source

Report actual clip name, duration, joint count, root translation and root rotation, whether mesh/skin/textures are embedded, and any visible intersections. The first Meshy exports can be maskless; we will test the existing full and half Grace attachments on the moving head in our viewer. Do not regenerate masks for each motion or promise mask clearance before that assembly check. Do not certify clearance from catalog previews. Inspect the full costume on this rig. Keep source motion intact; any in-place or clearance-corrected version must be a separately named derivative.

prompts.title: Signature actions · later/offline
prompts.text:
CATHEXIS — later signature actions on the accepted body and existing Grace mask

Stage 2 is closed. Full Grace, half Grace and the exposed original face are our complete appearance set for now. No new expression masks or facial rig. The motion bank can proceed without physical mask handling; these custom scenes are future work, not prerequisites for stage 3 or 4. Mask coverage is selected independently of the body motion. A half mask is a separate fitted coverage variant, not a claim that the full mask breaks or opens during a gesture.

These are custom briefs, NOT verified catalog entries. If your Agent interface cannot generate custom motions, state that and leave them pending. The Meshy Text-to-Motion API is a possible separate experiment; we can also author these offline. Neither route guarantees exact mask contact or costume clearance.

1. POISED IDLE (4–6 seconds, loop)
She settles onto one hip, raises her chin a fraction, slowly checks the audience and makes one small dismissive wrist flourish. Hold still long enough for the pause to feel intentional. Return seamlessly. No ordinary worker fidget or neutral breathing loop.

2. GRACE REVEAL (optional later, 5–7 seconds, one-shot)
She holds eye contact, raises a hand to the temple latch, grips the existing Grace faceplate, lifts it forward clear of the intact head and lowers it beside her shoulder. Hold the exposed original mechanism for a beat. The head never disappears or changes into a second face model. Hand contact, rigid mask trajectory and head-to-hand attachment transfer must be authored against the fitted prop offline. Do not treat Mirror_Viewing as a completed reveal.

3. GRACE RESEAT (optional later, staged against a known prop position)
She returns that same Grace mask to the head and settles it with a small decisive tilt. Preserve the prop continuously from hand to head, using authored contact markers. No selection from an expression-mask rack, new mask generation or automatic facial change. This replaces the abandoned mask-exchange action; it is not requested in the current Meshy batch.

4. INVITE ONE WORKER (4–6 seconds)
A measured turn toward one person, palm opened low, a teasing beckon, then an expectant hold. The worker may approach or refuse; Cathexis must not clap or celebrate regardless of the response. Exact partner placement is an offline paired scene.

5. DISMISS (3–4 seconds)
She looks the recipient up and down, tips her chin, turns one wrist in a small cutting dismissal and turns away before they finish answering. Precision and a held pause, not frantic waving.

6. HOLD THE ROOM / RALLY (6–8 seconds)
She collects attention with a small raised hand, opens her arms in a measured expansion, singles out an imagined listener and ends on one emphatic cue. Strong silhouette readable from CCTV. Crowd response is separate and driven by the simulation.

7. GRIEF AS PERFORMANCE (5–7 seconds)
A hand suspended near the chest, a long bowed head, a controlled opening toward the audience as if asking them to witness a loss. Choose full/half Grace or exposed mechanism independently; grief must read through the body performance without a dedicated grief mask. No guaranteed sincerity encoded in the clip.

8. THE LINE IS BENEATH ME (5–7 seconds)
At a waist-height station she approaches reluctantly, touches the object with exaggerated distaste, recoils and inspects or wipes dirt from her fingers. Provide a continuation that resumes the attempt with obvious resentment, and a separate refusal/appeal ending. This is not automatically a failed task: original conveyor success art still shows her dirty and angry. Exact object contact and task outcome remain our responsibility.

9. LOSING THE AUDIENCE (6–8 seconds)
An invitation receives no response. She repeats it more broadly, freezes when it fails, brings a hand near the temple as if checking her presentation and lets the pose collapse. Keep the gesture clear of both full and half Grace; an actual touch requires offline contact cleanup. Preserve a readable attempt and recovery before any larger tantrum.

10. OFFENDED EXIT (locomotion with a stationary gesture)
A dismissive turn and look back lead into the approved Hot Walk. She does not run, hurry into another gait, or enter alert. Preserve attitude, heel and skirt clearance; authored starts/stops/turn blends must connect to Hot Walk. If danger prevents a safe walking route, the simulation must handle that situation rather than silently replacing the gait.

11. CONTAMINATED AT THE BREWERY (5–7 seconds)
She withdraws a sticky hand from a known vat-side task, holds it far away from the ivory dress, spreads the fingers and inspects the residue. A sharp recoil becomes an angry glance at a supervisor or worker. Keep a safe grasp/contact phase on the other hand if bracing against the vat. Author hand placement and the partner's position offline. Do not substitute fighting or a happy grin.

12. THE GALLERY IS TOLERABLE (5–7 seconds, loop with contact markers)
She makes a precise adjustment at the loom, rests her head languidly against one hand, checks the result with apparent boredom, and returns to a small exact adjustment. Fine motor skill is visible even when enthusiasm is absent. Match the actual loom handles; no generic hammering or heavy lifting.

13. SECURITY IS NOT MY CONCERN (4–6 seconds, staged exit)
She glances at a form, lets it fall with a dismissive wrist, turns her back on the checkpoint and leaves with an offended theatrical stride. The paper remains a real prop with a defined release point. Worker movement through the unattended post is a separate simulation response.

14. OVERWHELMED AT THE CONVEYOR (4–6 seconds)
The poised stance contracts. Both hands rise to the sides of the crown, shoulders lift and she holds a furious, distressed posture, then tries to regain composure. Her original mechanical face may be exposed or half-covered; no face deformation or new distressed mask is needed. No smiling, dancing, head impact or damage implied. Keep hand/crown, hair and forearm clearances. A separate angry confrontation can follow if the simulation selects it.

Exact-contact scenes will need finger-pose and costume cleanup; broad silhouette gestures can be auditioned with the exported wrist-level rig. No physical prop exchange is accepted solely because the bare skeleton resembles the action. Keep source takes and cleaned derivatives separate. Dirt follows actual exposure and can persist into a composed gesture; emotional recovery does not clean or repair the robot.

prompts.title: Room conditions · later material variants
prompts.text:
CATHEXIS — dirt appearances on the ACCEPTED shared body

Choose one of the neutral A-pose dirt references before this step. These images define a surface treatment; they are NOT separate characters or alternative anatomy. Keep the original mechanical face intact. Grace is the only separate mask, with full/half/exposed coverage handled in our app; do not paint porcelain over the bare mechanical face or bake a mask onto the body.

Preserve the exact accepted body mesh, UVs, skeleton, skin weights and sockets. If your tools cannot preserve them, provide texture references for offline work instead of remeshing. A newly generated dirty body cannot be assumed to share the rig or animation files.

Stage condition: worn cracked ivory, antique brass and black mechanics. She is already aged, not glossy factory-new plastic.

Conveyor condition: dense charcoal soot and black-brown machine oil over much of the pale porcelain, cuffs, fingers, bodice and skirt. Darkened matted cable hair. Black-gray stained skirt with sparse pale edges. Use original conveyor art as the benchmark, not a few decorative splashes. The three A-pose options explore dry soot, wet oil and caked mixed grime; the owner will choose or combine them.

Brewery condition: later retexture using wet olive/green-brown process residue on hands, cuffs, bodice and hem. No fluid simulation or extra body geometry needed. Prepare after the conveyor treatment is chosen; do not infer approval from earlier posed concept sketches.

Keep amber eye/canister identity. No new injury, missing pieces, enlarged armor or combat redesign. No baked scenery, lighting or animation pose in textures. Export named material/texture variants; preserve clean source maps. Report any topology/UV changes honestly.

Dirt, full/half/exposed Grace coverage and body acting are independent presentation choices. No angry face model or facial rig is requested. If a dirty Grace surface is later needed, provide matching texture variants for the EXISTING Grace UVs as a separate task; both full and half coverage reuse those maps. She can be dirty and composed, clean and furious. Actual contamination follows exposure events and does not reset when changing rooms. This brief does not add cleaning or repair gameplay.

prompts.title: Delivery order and checks
prompts.text:
CURRENT ACCEPTED BODY: Cathexis_Body_v2_50k, 51,034 triangles. Rear skirt and appearance accepted on 14 October. Do not regenerate it. Start 03-rig-tests.txt with a matching normal-map export and neutral rig plus Hot Walk/expressive sway. Only the final body version belongs in the public viewer.

CATHEXIS — delivery order and remaining gates
1. Preserve the accepted v2 A-pose. Keep the original mechanical face intact under Grace; no facial-insert cutout.
2. Stage 2 is CLOSED: the owner has abandoned its remaining face-generation work. Existing Grace plus the original body face are sufficient. The app supplies full Grace, a clipped half and exposed mechanism. Do not wait for additional masks, expression inserts, facial bones or blendshapes.
3. Rig the accepted v2 BODY ONLY with its mechanical face rigidly following the head: first Hot Walk and expressive sway, then the two remaining tests in 03-rig-tests. Keep Grace out of the skinned export; report the head joint so our app can fit it. Inspect skirt/hair/arm/heel clearance, then test the moving head with existing full/half Grace locally. Report actual finger bones; wrist-only articulation is acceptable for these first tests.
4. After approval, audition the 28 priority motions, then useful candidates from the broader 161-entry name/category inventory. These are not 161 validated CATHEXIS clips. Use only Hot Walk for travel; no running or alert fallback. An expressive catalog name is not proof of the intended performance.
5. Select grime treatment A/B/C before material variants. They are comparison inputs, not three new bodies. Keep the same mesh, UVs and rig; brewery residue can be authored after the material direction is chosen. Dirt can accompany anger without forcing it in every scene.
6. Download original full sources privately, plus neutral and animated textured GLB/FBX. Preserve per-clip names/IDs and actual embedded inventories. All Animations may omit later jobs: verify local files, export missing clips separately.

Custom/offline gaps: sticky-finger disgust, protecting the skirt from grime, optional removal/reseating of the same Grace mask, precise conveyor/vat/loom contacts, Hot Walk starts/stops and paired worker responses. Expression-mask exchange is abandoned; physical mask handling does not block the motion bank. Do not substitute arbitrary gestures or claim these are finished by catalog retargeting.

The v2 body appearance and simplified face-system scope are accepted. Static full/half/exposed previews exist. Moving mask/costume clearance, rigging and gameplay integration remain unvalidated; facial articulation is outside the current scope. A/B/C material selection can wait until the rig tests.

prompts.text:
CATHEXIS — intact mechanical head with removable Grace coverage
STAGE 2 CLOSED — owner decision, 14 October 2026. The remaining face-generation work is abandoned. Use the accepted v2 body and existing Grace 3k/8k masks; the current assets are sufficient. This is a design/rebuild record, not a new Meshy task. Continue with stage 3.

The body owns its original mechanical grimace, skull, crown, hair and amber eyes. Keep all body geometry intact. Grace fits on top as a separate rigid porcelain shell. Three appearances: full Grace, half Grace exposing the original face, or exposed mechanism alone. Distress and sinister intent use this original mechanical face plus theatrical body acting; no dedicated mechanical expression bank is needed.

The viewer derives either half directly from the Grace mesh, preserving UVs and adding a narrow cut edge. Fit the shell close to the head without intersections, floating side gaps or a protruding far eye. The covered side is reviewable in both orientations. This is a static appearance test, not a finished removal animation or facial rig.

If Grace must be rebuilt later, generate one hollow porcelain faceplate with open eye apertures and a thin seating rim, using 04-mask-grace. No eyes, skull, hair, crown or neck. Preserve a master plus a lightweight 3k and closer-review 8k candidate, with actual counts and matching PBR maps. Keep textures and geometry independent of baked glow. Fit against the accepted body before replacing the runtime asset.

Grimace, Fury, Distress, the larger porcelain family and the separate half-shell illustration are earlier design studies. Do not generate them from this delivery brief. They remain references in the archive; the current split mask comes from Grace itself. Exact mask-hand contacts and the future head-bone attachment belong to offline assembly after the body rig passes.

prompts.title: Full body rebuild · reference only
prompts.text:
REBUILD REFERENCE ONLY. The accepted v2 body and skirt are already complete. Do not rerun this stage or the completed skirt repair. Stage 2 is closed; current work starts at 03-rig-tests.txt. The instructions below apply only if a complete body rebuild is explicitly requested.

Create CATHEXIS for Loopforge from the THREE attached body reference images: 01-cathexis-body-front.260b685edbc8b769.jpg, 02-cathexis-back-worn-cloth.f46b50f5d702ac1d.jpg and 03-cathexis-left-worn-cloth.5ca90f61805e55e6.jpg.

This task is the BODY ONLY. Do not install a porcelain face mask. Separate masks will follow as separate assets. Do not infer additional characters from any reference sheet.

Identity: a theatrical robot diva who runs the Burn-in Theatre. Cracked ivory armor, black articulated mechanics, antique brass corset ribs, compact diadem/headset, amber eye emitters and hip canisters, a compact back reactor, grouped cable-hair and a distressed open-front layered skirt. Elegant, commanding and unmistakably mechanical. Preserve the approved body proportions and high-heeled mechanical feet. Do not turn her into a worker, a glossy generic android, a princess or a weapon-bearing fighter.

Keep the accepted original mechanical face as permanent body geometry, including its grimace, skull, crown, hair and amber eyes. Grace is a separate porcelain shell that fits over this intact head. Do not cut away the original face, create a second mechanical expression insert or fuse the mask into the body. The same head supports full Grace, half Grace and exposed mechanism.

She is physically delicate and made for performance and fine interaction, not coarse industrial labor. Keep fine hands, porcelain and elegant costume. Later oil/soot and brewery-residue appearances will reuse this EXACT model, UVs and rig. Do not create a heavier dirty-body replacement. Anger and distress will be expressed through the exposed body face and acting, independent of dirt or mask coverage.

Generate the complete unrigged visual master first, in a clean symmetric A-pose. Hands clear of the torso, five separate mechanical fingers with a distinct thumb, legs and feet separated. The front view is the authority for proportions. Use the rear for reactor/hair construction and the profile for depth. Resolve minor view disagreements coherently rather than duplicating parts.

Keep fabric clear of legs and hands. The skirt has the original layered side panels and an open front. Its central rear cloth must form a continuous section behind the legs, reaching the lower ankles without knee/shin intersections. The revised back and matching left profile govern rear coverage and skirt material: mostly solid weathered gray-ivory cloth, restrained repaired seams and frayed edges, with excessive decorative lace removed. Preserve the original front opening, layered silhouette and crown. The original front drawing predates the fabric revision: use it for body proportions and the front opening, not the older ornate lace. In the left-facing profile, the rear panel is on the right and the leg is visible through the front opening. No floor train or knee-shaped cutouts. Hair is grouped into a few controllable locks/cable bundles, not thousands of separate strands. Do not bake background shadows, ambient glow, fog, transparent veils or magical energy into geometry. Surface cracks, weave and fine wear should primarily be texture detail.

Where your tools support it, keep body, skirt panels and hair sections separable. Do not claim separate objects unless the exported file actually contains them. If segmentation is unsupported, say so and preserve the neutral master for our offline cleanup. Do not discard the costume just to make auto-rigging easier.

Deliver:
- Cathexis_Body_v1_master: full-detail unrigged source.
- Cathexis_Body_v1_50k: a derivative around 40,000–55,000 triangles, preserving silhouette, fingers, face seating rim and costume. Report the actual count rather than claiming the target was exact.
- Textured GLB and FBX, neutral A-pose, PBR base color, normal, roughness and metallic maps. 2K working textures are sufficient for the first trial; preserve higher-resolution source maps if available.
- A brief report of material slots, separate objects, pose and any likely rigging problems.

Stop before generating the large animation bank. We will inspect the body, fit a mask and test the rig first. Do not overwrite the master when remeshing.

prompts.title: Completed skirt repair · reference only
prompts.text:
COMPLETED REBUILD REFERENCE — the resulting v2 body was accepted on 14 October 2026. Do not rerun this revision on the accepted body. Current next step is 03-rig-tests.txt.

Create a separate revision of the existing Cathexis_Body_v1 model. Use the existing body as the authority for geometry and identity. The attached revised back and left-profile images guide changes restricted to the skirt. Preserve the original master and delivery model.

Fill the missing center-back section with continuous fabric reaching the lower ankles, just above the heels. Join/overlap it naturally beneath the existing layered panels. The cloth hangs BEHIND the thighs, knees and calves with physical clearance. Neither knee nor shin may punch through it. Do not make knee-shaped holes, two separate leg coverings or a narrow strip between exposed legs.

Match the two revised views: mostly solid faded gray-ivory theatrical cloth, darker recessed layers, worn weave, restrained repaired seams and irregular frayed edges. Reduce the excessive ornamental lace, crocheted perforations and bridal scallops across the skirt. Preserve its layered silhouette and restrained flare. This remains a delicate performer's worn stage costume, not a work apron, burlap sack or bell gown. This base fabric revision is separate from the later oil/soot/brewery material variants.

Keep the original FRONT opening and exposed mechanical heels. In the left-facing profile the rear cloth is on the RIGHT; the visible leg is seen through the front opening, not a new side or rear cutout. Do not add a floor train. The original front drawing governs body proportions and the front opening; its older lace treatment does not override the new back/profile fabric references.

Keep the body, proportions, face, crown, hair, reactor, arms, hands, hip hardware, legs and heels unchanged. Keep separate face-mask assets unchanged. Do not enlarge the crown, modify the face seat or regenerate the character in this skirt task.

If your tools cannot preserve the existing body while making these localized changes, report that limitation before proceeding. Do not substitute a whole-body regeneration. We can perform local mesh/material corrections offline.

Produce Cathexis_Body_v1_SkirtRevision as a textured unrigged GLB and FBX inspection candidate. Preserve scale and pose; preserve topology, UVs and materials outside the skirt where supported, and disclose any changes. Name the added panel separately where supported. Report actual triangle counts and included texture maps. Show front, side, rear and rear three-quarter inspection views before rigging. Do not generate an animation bank yet.

These images communicate garment intent, not dimensionally exact projections. Validate panel joins and body clearance in the 3D viewer before replacing the current model; animation clearance remains a separate gate.
